articles.seo_description: Chef's cheat sheet for buffet portion planning: per-person guidelines, sample menus for 6, 10, and 20-35 guests, seating layouts, and budget tips.

blocks.text: *Cheat sheet: How to calculate party food portions and avoid overspending* Planning a party menu is always a balance between generous hospitality and budget. How do you make sure the spread looks abundant and appetizing, all guests leave fully satisfied, and yet there aren't heaps of untouched food left after the event? Here is a straightforward professional chef's guide for a beautiful, delicious, and well-planned buffet reception. **The golden rule of great hosting: guests remember the overall atmosphere, aesthetic presentation, variety of flavors, and your great mood - not endless kilograms of leftover food!** *How many appetizers are needed per person* The quantity of food directly depends on the event format, time of day, and whether a full hot entree is served: >1. __For a welcome reception or outdoor ceremony arrival (30-60 minutes):__ __3-7 appetizers__ per person are sufficient. The goal of the welcome zone is to greet guests with a glass of beverage and light hors d'oeuvres before the main program. >2. __For a standard cocktail buffet or banquet (2-4 hours):__ plan for __6-12 appetizers__ per guest. >3. __If the event lasts longer than 4 hours or runs without a hearty hot entree:__ plan for __12-18 appetizers__ per person. If you prefer not to calculate manually, try our free interactive menu planning tool!

*Ready-to-use scenarios by guest count* To make the buffet table look balanced, it is essential to combine textures and flavors: crisp baguettes, delicate mousses, savory meats and seafood delicacies, fresh vegetables, and artisan desserts. *Buffet reception for 6 guests (dinner party, family gathering, birthday)* Recommended volume: __40-60 appetizers__ (an average of 6-10 pieces per guest). An optimal spread includes: >1. __2-3 types of bruschetta or crostini:__ crisp crostini are easy to enjoy in one bite, while bruschetta provides an elevated restaurant-style presentation. Browse options in Bruschetta & Crostini. >2. __2-3 types of canapes:__ convenient bite-sized skewer presentations from Canapes & Bites. >3. __2-3 types of tartlets:__ savory fillings featuring pates, caviar, whipped cheese mousse, or poultry in Canapes & Bites. >4. __1-2 warm items:__ baked juliennes or savory entrees from Hot Dishes. >5. __Artisan cheese or charcuterie platter:__ fine cheeses paired with nuts and honey from Buffet & Appetizers. >6. __Salad:__ 1 fresh salad (Greek or Caesar) during warmer months, or a richer layered option in autumn and winter from Salads. >7. __Desserts:__ cupcakes, trifles, macarons, or mini pastries for tea and coffee from Desserts. *Celebration for 10 guests (friends party or department team gathering)* Recommended: __60-100 appetizers__ (6-10 pieces per guest). The perfect balance for an abundant table: >1. Bruschetta and crostini (with salmon, roast beef, or sun-dried tomatoes) - 2-3 varieties. >2. Canapes on skewers - 3-4 varieties. >3. Savory tartlets - 2-3 varieties. >4. Appetizing warm rolls (eggplant, zucchini, ham) and hot baked juliennes. >5. Individual portioned salads in cups from Salads. >6. Bite-sized buffet sweets from Desserts. If you want to save time, consider our curated value assortments in Buffet & Appetizers.

*Intimate wedding or anniversary for 20-35 guests* A larger family or wedding reception calls for a more substantial menu structure. We recommend planning for __10-15 appetizers per guest__, along with soup, a hearty hot entree, salads, and charcuterie platters. A balanced banquet-buffet lineup includes: >1. __First course:__ light broth with handmade noodles in spring, refreshing cold soups in summer, velvety pumpkin bisque with tiger prawns in autumn, or wild mushroom cream soup with garlic croutons in winter. >2. __Main hot entree with side dish:__ roasted meats, fish steaks, skewers, or braised specialties from Hot Dishes. >3. __Buffet section:__ 3 varieties of bruschetta (salmon, roast beef, prawn) from Bruschetta & Crostini, warm juliennes and rolls from Hot Dishes, and 3-5 varieties of canapes and tartlets from Canapes & Bites. >4. __Salads and platters:__ 150-200 grams of fresh salads per guest from Salads, plus meat, fish, cheese, and seasonal fruit platters from Buffet & Appetizers. >5. __Showstopper centerpieces:__ exclusive delicacy presentation for the head table from our Premium collection. >6. __On-site banquet setup:__ linens, professional tableware, tiered display stands, and decor coordination available via our interactive planner.

*Guest seating secrets and off-site events* Food placement and table styling depend directly on table arrangement in your venue: >1. __For U-shaped banquet tables:__ distribute dishes evenly across zones - 1-2 salads for every 3 sectors, with shared platters and canape trays duplicated along both long sides of the table so guests never have to reach across. >2. __For separate round or rectangular tables (6-10 guests each):__ each table must feature an identical setup, identical appetizers, salads, and beverages. This creates an inviting atmosphere and keeps dining comfortable for everyone. *Corporate events, conferences, and outdoor ceremonies* At networking events guests mingle on their feet, so the single-bite rule applies - appetizers must be individually portioned, neatly garnished, and comfortable to eat with one hand: >1. __For daytime brief receptions:__ 3-10 pieces per guest (depending on timing - from 30 minutes to 2 hours). >2. __For evening outdoor receptions:__ 10-15 pieces per guest. >3. __Most convenient options:__ salad shots in mini glasses, skewers, crostini, and bite-sized desserts from Canapes & Bites and Desserts. >4. __Kids area:__ if children attend the celebration, be sure to include kid-approved favorites from our Kids Menu (mini burgers, chicken nuggets, and fruit skewers).

*Which appetizers guests eat first* Years of professional catering experience demonstrate that the fastest items to disappear from the spread are: >1. Lightly salted salmon and tiger prawn appetizers from Bruschetta and Canapes. >2. Tender sous-vide roast beef bruschetta with sun-dried tomatoes. >3. Tartlets with creamy cheese and red caviar from Canapes & Bites. >4. Aromatic hot baked juliennes from Hot Dishes. >5. Signature chef specialties with creative culinary presentation. *How to avoid overspending on event catering* >1. __Avoid relying only on heavy dishes:__ an excess of dense food tires guests, leaving half the food uneaten on plates. >2. __Focus on varied bite-sized finger foods rather than oversized platters:__ curated gastrobuffet boxes look modern, save budget, and are enjoyed with far greater enthusiasm. >3. __Consider your guest demographics:__ for hearty gatherings, plan 20-30% more meat and warm dishes; for brunch, showers, and business coffee breaks, emphasize crisp greens, poultry, seafood, and fresh fruit. >4. __Take advantage of combinations:__ value sets in Buffet & Appetizers are always more economical than ordering single positions individually. >5. __Elevate the presentation:__ aesthetic table decor and multi-tiered risers visually enrich the spread even on a modest budget. **Chef's recommendation: submit an estimate request online or reach out - we will calculate exact portions and provide 2 custom menu concepts tailored to your event format and budget!**
